question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $16,$ the additive inverse of $45$ modulo $16$ is{{field-1}}.

current_example.problem: Find the additive inverse of $23$ modulo $15.$
current_example.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $23$ modulo $15$ is the integer $0 \leq x \lt 15$ such that

$$
x + 23 \equiv 0 \quad (\textrm{mod}\:15).
$$

First, we note that $23\equiv 8\:(\textrm{mod}\:15){:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}23 & ≡1\cdot 15+8 & \,(\text{mod}\,15) \\  & ≡1\cdot 0+8 & \,(\text{mod}\,15) \\  & ≡8 & \,(\text{mod}\,15)\end{aligned}
$$

Also, note that $-8 + 8 \equiv 0,$ so $x\equiv -8\:(\textrm{mod}\:15).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-8 & \,(\text{mod}\,15) \\  & ≡0-8 & \,(\text{mod}\,15) \\  & ≡15-8 & \,(\text{mod}\,15) \\  & ≡7 & \,(\text{mod}\,15)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $23$ modulo $15$ is $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}7}.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}23+7≡30≡2\cdot 15≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,15)\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a \: \textrm{mod} \: n.$
